messages:
Maria: Heads up — reproducible flake when bringing up new judge v3-small on eval-runner.
Kevin: what flake?
Maria: metric ordering changes between runs, e.g., A ties B in run1, B wins in run2.
Maria: Stack: eval-runner v0.9.2, judge v3-small quantized-int8, dataset: rub_test_2026
Ashley: do you have logs or seed?
Maria: pasted minimal trace: 
```
2026-03-12T14:02:11Z eval-runner INFO run_id=abc123 sample_idx=42 rand_seed=0x1f2a
2026-03-12T14:02:11Z judge INFO choice=[B]
2026-03-12T14:03:01Z eval-runner INFO run_id=def456 sample_idx=42 rand_seed=0x1f2a
2026-03-12T14:03:01Z judge INFO choice=[A]
```
Kevin: same seed? looks like nondeterministic ordering in batch processing.
Sara: could be kv-cache padding or async batch boundary.
Dave: I remember a batching change in v0.9.2 that shuffles within micro-batches for perf — maybe it leaked into deterministic eval mode.
Maria: config I'm using:
```
{ "mode": "eval", "batch_policy": "micro-batch", "deterministic": true, "rng_seed": 12345 }
```
Ashley: deterministic flag respected? I thought we only honored it in hosted path.
Maria: tried both `deterministic=true` and explicit rng_seed, same flips.
ci-bot: run 1823334444 triggered: eval-harness/runner#245 flaky-sample-check.
Kevin: can we reproduce locally with single-threaded runner? if it stops flipping then it's a concurrency issue.
Maria: single-threaded still flips, but frequency drops.
Dave: could be quantization nondeterminism in judge inference (int8 kernel uses atomic ops?).
Sara: quick experiment: re-run with `quant_backend=fp16` or `disable_async_kernels=true`.
Maria: did fp16 — flips disappeared. seems tied to int8 path.
Ashley: filing a ticket for quant kernel determinism, cc @eng-runtime.
Maria: in meantime propose heuristic: tie-breaker should include deterministic tie hash: e.g., hash(sample_id + model_name) to break ties reproducibly.
Kevin: agreed, do it in eval-harness as fallback.
Maria: created PR draft: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/512> (wip).
Dave: also add a smoke CI that runs judge onboarding with both int8/fp16 to catch regresses.
ops-bot: scheduled nightly job: eval-smoke/compare-quant-variants.
Maria: thanks — will follow up with perf cost numbers after more runs :pray:
